mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -76% over the last two weeks, indicating a floor in commuting suppression. This plateau signals that further workplace closures are unlikely, permitting gradual retail reopening as essential-worker routines normalize, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -51.7% to -76.0% then stabilized at -76.0% over t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility falls below -80% in any week of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains below -75% for all four weeks ahead.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen consistently from +22.1% to +31.1% over four weeks, indicating sustained home confinement compliance. This behavioral lock-in suppresses discretionary retail visits through habit formation and reduced outdoor exposure tolerance, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from +22.1% to +31.1% over four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below +25% in any week of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -60% in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations have collapsed to -79.4%, a threshold indicating near-total public transport shutdown. When transit falls below -75%, retail footfall cannot recover because customers cannot reach retail venues. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed until TRANSIT recovers above -50%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -75% and remains there for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -79.4% in t-0w, lowest observed level
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -50% within the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -70%, contradicting the immobility constraint.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -38.4% to -17.7% over two weeks, signaling outdoor activity resumption. This outdoor substitution effect reduces demand for indoor retail venues, as consumers redirect discretionary time to parks. RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as PARKS recovery continues.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -20% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -38.4% at t-2w to -17.7% at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls back below -25% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -70% while PARKS remains above -20%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized at -37.7% while RETAIL_REC collapsed to -82.0%, revealing a two-tier consumer behavior: essential shopping continues at reduced levels, but discretionary retail is abandoned. This bifurcation persists because essential-goods demand is inelastic while retail demand is highly elastic to lockdown severity. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed relative to GROCERY_PHARM over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC minus GROCERY_PHARM spread exceeds -44 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -82.0% vs GROCERY_PHARM at -37.7% at t-0w, a 44.3 point gap
failure_condition: The RETAIL_REC to GROCERY_PHARM gap narrows to less than 30 percentage points within four weeks, indicating convergence toward normal shopping patterns.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both declined sharply and stabilized at -76% and -79% respectively, indicating synchronized economic shutdown. This dual suppression of commuting and workplace access creates a demand vacuum for retail. RETAIL_REC will remain at floor levels (-80% or lower) as long as both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -70%, because neither workers nor transit users can generate retail footfall.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -70% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -76.0% and TRANSIT at -79.4% at t-0w, both sustained below -70% for two weeks
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT recovers above -60% within the next four weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -75%, breaking the synchronized suppression assumption.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-April in London marks the onset of spring weather and Easter holiday periods. Historically, this seasonal window drives outdoor recreation and holiday travel. PARKS recovery from -38.4% to -17.7% reflects this seasonal pull. Seasonal demand will shift consumer time away from indoor retail toward outdoor activities and holiday destinations, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed despite any policy relaxation.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises above -15% during April-May seasonal window
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -17.7% at t-0w (mid-April), showing seasonal recovery trajectory
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below -25% in any week of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -60% while PARKS remains above -15%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen to +31.1%, indicating enforced home confinement. TRANSIT has collapsed to -79.4%, indicating transport restrictions. When both RESIDENTIAL is elevated (>+25%) and TRANSIT is severely suppressed (<-75%), retail recovery is mechanically blocked: people are confined at home and cannot reach retail venues. RETAIL_REC will remain below -75% until TRANSIT recovers above -60% OR RESIDENTIAL falls below +20%.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +25% AND TRANSIT below -75% simultaneously for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +31.1% and TRANSIT at -79.4% at t-0w, both conditions met for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -70% in any week while both RESIDENTIAL remains above +25% and TRANSIT remains below -75%, violating the mechanical immobility constraint.
